Name: Adult Gay Male 18+ Friendship Circle
Resource Description:
‍This friendship circle is for adults (18+) that identify as gay and male.

Friendship Circles? 

These groups are designed to provide a connection with folx you identify with and help you manage the trials you encounter every day. Friendship Circles create an opportunity for you to take control and thrive in your own life. Friendship Circles provide opportunities for sharing, connection, and support by discussing issues and experiences relevant to each group, often exploring the intersectionality of conservative cultures, spirituality, sexuality, social issues, transitional issues, and health issues and how it impacts us. The groups also provide a great support network—members in similar circumstances with similar feelings with whom they can share in an open and unedited fashion. 

Groups organized by sexuality, age, and/or gender identity.

For schedules and more information, please visit your nearest Encircle House website.

Name: Advanced Awareness Counseling
Resource Description:
We consist of a network of qualified mental health providers who have been selected for outstanding educational credentials, experience in the field, exceptional client care principles, high integrity, and expertise in particular areas of specialty.

Our various practitioners have proficiency in faith transitions, minority concerns, marriage counseling, couples counseling, family therapy, PTSD and trauma-related conditions (including EMDR therapy), generalized anxiety and social anxiety, gender dysphoria, gender and transgender specialized care, depression, suicide prevention, bipolar disorder, borderline personality disorder, adolescents and children, play therapy, sand tray therapy, anger management, grief and loss, and much more.

Our facility and our counselors are an ally to the LGBTQ+ community, and we provide support and affirming counseling for individuals of all orientations, identities, races, ethnicities, etc.

We specialize in working with gender non-conforming/transgender clients, including non-binary, gender questioning and/or exploring, and any and all identities along the spectrum.

Our gender therapists are trained in the WPATH (World Professional Association for Transgender Health) standards of care and engage in continual training via the LGBT Affirmative Therapists Guild of Utah and WPATH.

We are licensed by the Department of Human Services as a state and court-approved domestic violence and substance abuse provider, offering domestic violence assessments, domestic violence counseling, substance abuse assessments, and substance abuse counseling. 

We believe in helping our clients live authentically and by their own truth. Our team members are effective in identifying the underlying causes of your concerns and moving forward with a productive, results-oriented resolution along with supportive empathy. Our counselors are trained in suicide prevention and assessment. They have a deeply vested interest in helping anyone who has ever experienced suicidal ideation and many of the pains and burdens that come with that. 

Our staff is professional and open-minded and will not steer you down any rigid "conventional" path or with any pre-determined societal or religious boundaries. We are respectful of your uniqueness, and we are dedicated to helping you with your progression in a way that fits your unique personality, values, and expectations. 

We believe in advocating for our clients and will do everything in our power to do so!

Name: BW Bastian Foundation
Resource Description: The B.W. Bastian Foundation strives to build community and understanding by supporting local and national institutions. Financial support is directed to the Arts through educational outreach. A strong commitment is placed on programs and organizations that benefit, encourage, and preserve the rights of individuals, promote equality for the LGBTQ+ community and HIV/AIDS programs. The B.W. Bastian Foundation only supports organizations who wholeheartedly embrace the principle of equality. As such, each organization must include a statement specifically stating their commitment to equality for all Americans, including the gay and lesbian community, in their application.

Name: BYU USGA
Resource Description:
Welcome to USGA! 

Understanding Sexuality, Gender, and Allyship (USGA) is an unofficial group of Brigham Young University students, faculty, and guests who wish to enhance the BYU community by providing a safe space for open, respectful conversation on LGBTQ & SSA topics. USGA is a place of refuge and our priority is to have compassion and to seek understanding through listening. Harassment or antagonism against any person or organization will not be tolerated. Members are asked to be mindful of USGA’s political neutrality and to be respectful of BYU, The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints, and the beliefs and experiences of others. In order to maintain a safe and welcoming environment, USGA supports its members in upholding the Honor Code, and expects all participants to be respectful of others’ names, pronouns, and identities. They encourage all not to make assumptions or ask others to unwillingly disclose their identity or beliefs. They also ask attendees to refrain from using USGA as a place for romantic or sexual pursuits.‍

Name: Cache Pride Center
Resource Description:
Cache Pride Center is a program of the Cache Valley Unitarian Universalists Church and is committed to transforming and supporting Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Queer, Pansexual, plus (LGBTQIAP+) Cache Valley communities through support groups, comprehensive programming, suicide prevention, mentoring, community advocacy, and community training devised to promote positive outlooks and changes within underserved populations. 

- Groups: Cache Pride Center has groups/programs for preteens, teens, transgender individuals, & LGBTQ+ adults.
- Parent Support: We know it is important for LGBTQ+ persons to have support. Cache Pride Center offers parent support group services
- We offer have other services for those in need of food, clothing, hygiene items, and temporary housing/shelter. 
- We assist in finding health care and mental health professionals.

Name: CDC National Info Hotline
Resource Description: CDC’s national health information hotline provides answers to your questions regarding HIV, how to protect yourself, and where to get an HIV test. In English, en Español, 8 am to 8 pm ET, Monday through Friday.

Name: Celebrate Therapy
Resource Description: Celebrate Therapy is the first clinic in Provo, Utah and the surrounding area that is owned and run by a team of queer clinicians. We work to support clients in becoming confident and supported in their own queerness. We’ll also work alongside family members who are working through how to support their queer loved ones. We are hoping to lead a transformational change Utah County and beyond!

Name: Cheer Salt Lake
Resource Description: Founded in 2011, Cheer Salt Lake raises funds and awareness for those living with life-challenging conditions in the LGBTQ community and beyond. We're an inclusive team that welcomes volunteers from all backgrounds and partners with a variety of community organizations in Salt Lake, Provo, and Ogden. We're a federal 501(c)3 non-profit and registered charity in the state of Utah.

Name: Children's Service Society of Utah
Resource Description: Children’s Service Society of Utah empowers families and caregivers through services that support the safety and well-being of children. CSS is the oldest non-denominational child welfare and family support agency in Utah. Through the years Children’s Service Society has evolved its programs according to the needs of the children and families they serve in the community. Today Children’s Service Society of Utah empowers families and caregivers through services that support the safety and well-being of children. This is accomplished through these programs: Adoption, Grandfamilies Kinship Care, Care About Childcare and Utah Parents in Action, Home Visitation.

Name: Cougar Pride
Resource Description: Cougar Pride Center aims to empower queer BYU students, celebrate progress, and advocate for change through collaborative activism. Founded in 2021, we are a volunteer-run organization that strives to create community and care for LGBTQ+ individuals on campus.

Name: Creating Community - LGBTQ & Allies
Resource Description: A space for LGBTQ people and their loved ones. We are here to share a connection, friendship, and support. We have a get-together on the fourth Sunday of each month in Davis County, Utah.

Name: Damn These Heels
Resource Description: The annual film festival explores LGBTQ issues, ideas, and art through showcasing dramatic and documentary films from around the world. Damn These Heels remains a community focused, grassroots, locally-produced festival with strong community partnerships.

Name: Dixie State LGBTQ+ Resource Center
Resource Description:
Our mission is to promote understanding and acceptance for all individuals by education, activities, and service for the campus and larger community. The club provides support and social networking for all persuasions of people. We want to raise awareness about suicide rates and promote education of homosexuality and acceptance for equality in Saint George.

WHAT WE DO

The Resource Center empowers the LGBTQ+ people who are part of DSU’s community. Much of this comes from the simple act of providing information to everyone. Other parts of the center’s mission include scholarships, mentoring, promoting visibility and acceptance, and outreach. We create a space for students where they feel safe to gather, express themselves, discuss ideas, learn, and teach others. We work as a team to improve LGBTQ+ inclusion across campus.

- Education
- Safe Zone Training
- Mentoring Support
- Peer Support Groups
- LGBTQ+ Hosted Events
- Provide Resources (locally and nationally)
- Create Visibility
- Assist in finding LGBTQ+ scholarships
- Assist with filing name change documents or transition related documents
- And much more! (ask and we will help you with it)‍

Hours: Monday through Friday 11:30am-5pm

Name: Dragon Dads
Resource Description: We fight to prevent teen suicide and to provide support and education to other fathers who want to show love and support for their LGBTQIA+ children.If you would like more information or would like to join, please click below to begin the process.

Name: Emmaus LGBTQ Ministry
Resource Description:
Emmaus fosters and supports ministry to and with LGBTQ individuals and their families in and adjacent to The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

Emmaus is a community of heterosexual/cisgender and LGBTQ Latter-day Saints who are called to ministry for the safety, well-being and happiness of LGBTQ people in and adjacent to The Church of Jesus Christ.

We envision communities, congregations and families where LGBTQ individuals know they are cherished, where they are free from discrimination and inequality, where they are fully heard, understood and protected, and where their agency is respected.

We feel driven to do this work by our testimonies of the Gospel. We know there is a place in Christ’s Church and in our Heavenly Parents’ plan for every single one of us, and our hearts ache for the anguish caused by misunderstanding and lack of knowledge.

We believe that the way forward lies through relationship, connection and listening. We honor LGBTQ individuals’ courage, discernment process, and agency, and we are working for their nurture and support in every congregation, community and family. We want members and leaders of the Church to know LGBTQ individuals and to hear their stories. We want every LGBTQ individual to know that their contributions are indispensable, and to experience love in their church and in their families that is truly unconditional.

We recognize that real change takes time and requires patience. We know from experience the power of relationship to transform understanding. We are committed to a process that fosters connection, communication, learning, and empathy.

Name: Equality Utah
Resource Description:
Equality Utah works to build a community where every Utahn is valued for being who they are regardless of sexual orientation or gender identity. We believe everyone in our state deserves to be treated with respect and understanding and to be afforded the same basic freedoms and opportunities as everyone else.

OUR VISION: A fair and just Utah. OUR MISSION: To secure equal rights and protections for lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and queer Utahns and their families.

OUR ISSUES: 
Nondiscrimination
LGBTQ Families
Victim Targeting
LGBTQ Youth
Transgender Utahns
Suicide Prevention

Name: Family Acceptance Project
Resource Description: The Family Acceptance Project® is a research, intervention, education and policy initiative that works to prevent health and mental health risks for lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender (LGBTQ) children and youth, including suicide, homelessness, drug use and HIV – in the context of their families, cultures and faith communities. We use a research-based, culturally grounded approach to help ethnically, racially and religiously diverse families learn to support their LGBTQ children.Our team has put research into practice by developing an evidence-based family model of wellness, prevention and care to strengthen families and promote positive development and healthy futures for LGBTQ children and youth. We provide training and consultation on our family-based prevention and intervention approach across the United States and in other countries.‍

Resource Description: We offer a suite of patient-centered and evidenced-based programs that span a continuum of care across pre-treatment, treatment entry, recovery initiation, housing, employment, and long-term recovery management.

Name: Flourish Therapy
Resource Description: Flourish Therapy is a 501(c)(3) non -profit organization that provides subsidized therapy for LGBTQ clients and offers a wide variety of therapy options including: individual, couples, family and group counseling for all age groups, including short- and long-term counseling, crisis intervention, parent intervention, and support services with a focus on quality care for LGBTQ clients and their families. They finance more than 100 free sessions a month and 75% of their clients pay less than $50.00 per session. The clinical staff includes culturally competent licensed mental health practitioners, marriage and family therapists and counselors. Flourish works with several insurances, including Select Health, PEHP, EMI and DMBA.‍ Flourish Therapy is based in Utah county, with therapy services offered across, Utah, Davis, and Salt Lake counties.

Name: Food & Friends Cache Valley
Resource Description: We are a gay men's social group in the Cache Valley that meets monthly for dinner, conversation, board games, and/or movie nights. We meet on 2nd Saturday of every month at 6 PM either at a local restaurant (different restaurant each month) or at a member's house for potluck dinner. Join us to try food from different restaurants in Cache Valley while making new friends or catching up with old ones.We welcome all gay/bi/trans men, 18 yrs and up. We don't have to be residents of Cache Valley as we have friends from SLC that had attended our gatherings. We are a friendly, supportive and are nonjudgmental group of like-minded men who like trying different cuisines and have fun socializing. We ask that everyone be respectful as some of our members may not be "out".

Resource Description: The Facebook page listed below is a portal for the For the Strength of LGBTQ/SSA Youth Facebook group which is "Secret." The group is specifically for straight and LGBTQ/SSA LDS youth ages 12-18 to support one another and is moderated by LDS youth with the supervision of a few straight/cis parents and two LDS therapists. ‍If you are a youth age 12-18 and would like to join, leave a message with the page or email below.

Name: Full Circle Wellness Center
Resource Description: Full Circle Wellness Center host various monthly LGBTQ events at their center including yoga meetups, business cultural competency trainings, potlucks, etc. Full Circle Wellness Center is also an LGBTQ friendly business offering Ionic foot detox baths, reiki, foot zoning, light therapy, wellness related classes, meditation circles, nutritional therapy, message, tarot reading and health/wellness products.
Address: 60 S Main St Suite 101, Brigham City, UT 84302

Name: Gay Latter Day Saint Crossroads
Resource Description: Evan Smith believed the anti-gay messages he heard in church during his childhood, which contributed to some negative experiences on his mission in San Francisco. Later, as a bishop and then a counselor in a stake presidency,his heart softened as church members came to him seeking guidance about feeling attracted to others of the same gender. Evan’s investigating and study became personal when his own son came out as gay.In this navigable e-book, Evan tackles the issues with a lawyer’s mind and a penetrating analysis of scriptures and church doctrine. He addresses such questions as these: “What insights apply from the end of polygamy and the racebased priesthood/temple ban?” “Why do I stay in the church?” and, most importantly, “What words are hurtful/helpful to LGBTQ people and their families?”

Resource Description:

Thank you all for the love and support you offer to Genderbands as an organization. We couldn’t do what we do without you!

Name: GEM Stories
Resource Description:
GEM Stories seeks to amplify the voices of gender-expansive Mormons: Latter-day Saints or those adjacent to it, who are also transgender, agender, genderqueer, non-binary, intersex, two-spirit, or otherwise not cisgender.

This space cultivates support for those of us who are grappling, or have grappled, with tension between our genders, and the doctrines, teachings, and behaviors of LDS Church leaders and members. We acknowledge the unique joys and pains that come with existing in any capacity as a GE Mormon, and we affirm the spiritual paths and individual agency of every gender-expansive person.

Our hope is that in getting to know us better, LDS leaders and members can gain a greater understanding of how to minister to and love their GE siblings— and that other GE individuals will know that they aren't alone.

Name: GLSEN Northern Utah
Resource Description:
GLSEN Northern Utah is a chapter of GLSEN, a national organization fighting for every student’s right to a safe, supportive education. 

GLSEN Northern Utah is a grassroots initiative, working locally in our community to ensure safe schools for all students, regardless of sexual orientation and gender identity. There are 43 Chapters around the country doing this important work. Join us today!
Our chapter supports students and educators locally, organizes around LGBTQ-affirming public policy, plans teacher trainings, and hosts events for students, educators, parents, and allies. Chapters like ours play an important role in bringing GLSEN’s programs and visions to right where we live, work, and learn. While some chapters have full-time or part-time staff, most are entirely volunteer-based. We're always looking for new volunteers to help us ensure safe schools for all students.

Name: Health Insurance Provider Search
Resource Description: Use the following links below to find in-network providers within your health insurance plan.

Name: Help Me Flourish: Parent and Caregiver Support Group
Resource Description:
Christine Hubbard, Social Work Associate at Flourish Therapy, hosts an educational support group for parents and caregivers of LGBTQIA youth. 6 Topics. 1.5 hours a week to talk and learn. Need support and knowledge? Register below!

 Topics include: 

1- Basics of Gender and Sexual Identity

2- Body Image and Development of Self Esteem

3- How to Talk to Your LGBTQIA Kids About Sex

4- Helping Your Kids Build a Support Network 

5- Coping As Parents

Name: Human Rights Campaign
Resource Description: Our Mission: By inspiring and engaging individuals and communities, the Human Rights Campaign strives to end discrimination against LGBTQ people and realize a world that achieves fundamental fairness and equality for all. HRC envisions a world where lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and queer people are ensured equality and embraced as full members of society at home, at work and in every community.

Name: I'll Walk With You
Resource Description: These videos were created for Latter-day Saint parents and allies to voice their love for their LGBT brothers and sisters, sons and daughters. They want to give a message of comfort and support to other parents who are navigating the difficult conflicts that can arise in families around this issue. Each video offers a unique perspective, but all of the participants are united in a concern for individuals and families who might be struggling and even suffering because of misunderstandings. The participants are also united in the belief that their LDS religion offers them the tools to resolve these problems in a way that allows for health and growth of each member of the family and preserves the unity and strength of family bonds. Most of these families are also willing to communicate with parents and individuals who are looking for advice and support. If you are new to this issue or if you feel alone or isolated and need to talk to a Mormon parent who has gone through these experiences, please send us an email.

Name: It Gets Better
Resource Description: In 2012, gay BYU students from the Understanding Same-Gender Attraction (USGA) group created the “It Gets Better” video series in order to promote conversation and understanding for those with same-sex attraction on campus. Kendall Wilcox, a former employee at BYUtv and (at the time) member of the USGA stated “The primary intent [of the video] was to just send a message of love, hope and community to LGBT Mormon youth who are at their most vulnerable, who may be questioning their self-worth and their status before God. . . We want this video to send the message that there is hope, they have a future, there is hope for love and happiness in the future.”‍

Name: Journeys of Faith
Resource Description:
The Journeys of Faith Project features the personal stories of Latter-day Saint individuals and families addressing gender identity or transgenderism who are striving to find congruence and peace within the context of faith in the gospel of Jesus Christ.

Their stories allow each of us a glimpse into their inner experience, inviting us into a place of greater awareness and empathy for an aspect of the human experience so personal and poignant to some of our brothers and sisters. As they struggle to address a difficult and complex issue with few answers, and as we walk with them on their personal journeys, they remind us what it means to live by faith.

Name: Journeys Online Community
Resource Description: Affirmation Journeys is a group oriented toward LGBTQIA, their families, and allies who are transitioning out of Mormon orthodoxy, as well as former Mormons. We welcome everybody, but the discussions will be from a perspective of those who are either Mormons undergoing a faith transition, unorthodox Mormons, non-believing Mormons or former Mormons. The group will be open to all topics of particular interest to this community, but it will have a particular goal of helping people move forward in healthy productive ways as they proceed during or following a faith transition.‍

Name: LGBTQ & Allied Lawyers of Utah
Resource Description: LGBT & Allied Lawyers of Utah is a group of lawyers serving lawyers. We are an association of the Utah State Bar and an affiliate of the National LGBT Bar Association. Our mission is to use education and advocacy to promote and support the rights of LGBT people within the legal profession and throughout Utah.We are sometimes contacted by people who are seeking legal advice or looking to hire an attorney who specializes in LGBTQ issues. We have created this directory to assist these potential clients. The attorneys listed below represent clients on LGBTQ issues. Name: LGBTQ Adult Friendship Circle
Resource Description:
This friendship circle is for adults (25+) that identify as LGBTQ+.

Friendship Circles?
These groups are designed to provide connection with folx you identify with and help you manage the trials you encounter every day. Friendship Circles create an opportunity for you to take control and thrive in your own life.

Friendship Circles provide opportunities for sharing, connection, and support through discussion of issues and experiences relevant to each group, often exploring the intersectionality of conservative cultures, spirituality, sexuality, social issues, transitional issues, and health issues and the ways it impacts us. The groups also provide a great support network—members in similar circumstances with similar feelings with whom they can share in an open and unedited fashion. 

Groups organized by sexuality, age, and/or gender identity.

For schedules and more information please visit your nearest Encircle House website.

Name: LGBTQ Affirmative Therapist Guild of Utah
Resource Description: The LGBTQ-Affirmative Psychotherapist Guild of Utah is a Utah-based, grassroots organization of licensed mental-health professionals and students-in-training. We share a collaborative commitment to make affirmative culturally competent therapy available for anyone.The Guild believes that all individuals and families deserve mental health services that affirm sexual and gender diversity. To this end, we provide innovative and affirmative training to mental health professionals and trainees grounded in values of cultural humility, social advocacy, collaboration, and inclusivity. We believe this work honors and celebrates the lived experiences of sexual and gender diverse individuals, families, and communities while promoting justice and dignity.‍LGBTQ Affirming Therapist DirectoryA directory of self-reported LGBTQ Affirmative therapists in Utah. http://www.lgbtqtherapists.com/directory.html‍Other ServicesRun CE Programs: Our Leaderships Team develops ideas for training based on community need and professional resources. We organize, plan, schedule and run 18 CE hours a year, including a bi-annual ethics program where you can earn the 6 hours of required ethics CEs for the two-year licensing cycle.Organize Political Actions: The Guild participates in community events such as the Pride Parade and other community based social justice actions.Provide Community Training: Members of the guild provide training and resources to interested community partners in an effort to raise awareness and skills in the broader Utah region.

Name: LGBTQ and Allies in Wards, Stakes and Missions
Resource Description:
This is a group of active Latter-day Saints (LGBTQ, Allies and Local Leaders) who are working in Ward, Stake, Seminaries and Institutes, Church Schools, or Mission Leadership to put together LGBTQ meetings, firesides, FHEs, materials, class discussions, Church talks, etc.

The purpose is to share ideas, materials, approaches, events so that each person does not feel they are starting from scratch or alone in their efforts.
President Ballard asked us to council together—and this virtual group gives us a chance to do that—and come up with the right plan/approach for your area of influence.
It is not a place to debate Church doctrine or policy.

Posts not focused on this topic will be removed (sorry my friends, but really want to keep the focus on the mission statement).
You are welcome to invite others to the group. Remind them to answer the two questions that are required to join the group (active LDS and follow group mission).

Thank you,
Richard Ostler🙏

Resource Description:
To increase awareness and education concerning LGBTQIA+ healthcare issues as well as provide a social and support network for University of Utah medical students, health sciences students, residents, and faculty who identify as LGBTQIA+.
Need a safe space? Head to the "Synapse" in the basement of the Health Sciences Library. This space is designed for students to have a place to go where they can feel comfortable, relax, or study. There are couches, coffee makers, and plenty of study spaces available!

Name: Lift + Love
Resource Description:
My husband, Kenn, and I live in Salt Lake and have three amazing children and a brand-new son-in-law We are a regular LDS LGBTQ family.

As the mother of an LGBTQ child and a member of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints, I have learned to rely on the Lord and trust the Inspiration I received. My goal is to keep all of my children connected to their Savior and to teach them to face life with courage and confidence

I learned this growing up in my own LGBTQ family. My oldest brother, Preston was gay. Raising a gay child in the 70s and 80s my parents were on their own to navigate what it meant to be an openly gay family in the church. It was not easy and neither they nor my brother felt supported. But they did the best they could

In 2017, my brother took his own life. At the same time, my oldest son was starting his own process of coming out. My brother's painful life was a total gift to me. Through the good and the bad, the sad and the joyful, I learned what I needed to know to raise my son.

Because of the journey I have been on and the blessings that have come to our family, I wanted to do more to help other LGBTQ families and wards support these most precious children of our Heavenly Parents

The Lift Love instagram account ilftandloveorg and website liftandlove.org are meant to support teach and empower LGBTQ LDS families.

Name: Lift + Love LGBTQ+ Mamas (Parents) Community
Resource Description: We are excited to have you join this growing group of LDS mothers who want to raise healthy LGBTQ children.  There is wisdom in this community of faithful women and strength in knowing that you are not alone.

Resource Description: Affirmation Journeys is a group oriented toward LGBTQIA, their families, and allies who are transitioning out of Mormon orthodoxy, as well as former Mormons. We welcome everybody, but the discussions will be from a perspective of those who are either Mormons undergoing a faith transition, unorthodox Mormons, non-believing Mormons or former Mormons. The group will be open to all topics of particular interest to this community, but it will have a particular goal of helping people move forward in healthy productive ways as they proceed during or following a faith transition.‍

Name: Mama Dragons
Resource Description: About Us: Mama Dragons is a support organization for Mormon and former-Mormon mothers of LGBTQ children. Mama Dragons exist to inspire and empower mothers. We actively promote healthy, loving, and supportive environments for mothers of LGBTQIA children.Our Mission: We support, educate, and empower mothers of LGBTQ children.

Name: Mama Dragons Facebook Group
Resource Description:
This Mama Dragons Main Group on Facebook is the primary support group for all mothers of LGBTQ children navigating this sometimes challenging journey within their family and community. This group strives to be a space free of judgment between members and one that creates a safe place for conversation and support for individuals regardless of cultural or religious backgrounds. Mamas can ask questions, share success stories, share heartaches and heartbreaks, request and give advice, and bring a wealth of knowledge and experience to others in the group.

For more targeted needs and discussions, Mama Dragons also offers Facebook subgroups. Once you are a member of this main support group (or the Madres Dragones Facebook group), you can be invited – or request an invitation – to join other Mama Dragons subgroups listed below that meet your needs.

Name: Men Finding Peace - Salt Lake City
Resource Description:
What is Men Finding Peace?

More than a support group, more than a church meeting, Men Finding Peace is a group of men who share common goals and needs.  It is a place where men can be authentic and learn from other gay/SSA men from our everyday experiences, faith, and insight. To give strength to those who strive to live a covenant life of faith or those men who are just seeking peace and acceptance wherever they may be on their journey. It’s a place where ideas are shared to find strength, hope, and resolve with like men who share a common bond in brotherhood. A group that provides fellowship, purpose, and meaning through group sharing and other activities. 

The Men Finding Peace group meets every Wednesday at 7:00 pm until 8:30 pm. *Note current meetup information available on the Men Finding Peace Salt Lake City Facebook Group. 

*Disclaimer*: Men Finding Peace is an independent group not associated or affiliated with North Star International or the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints though we wholly accept and adopt their mission, doctrine, and values. Any opinions shared or expressed are strictly our own.

Name: Men Finding Peace - Utah Valley
Resource Description: More than a support group or a church meeting, “Men Finding Peace” is an independent group of men who share common goals, needs, and who want to participate in a gospel-oriented and positive association. It serves as a forum where men can learn from each other what it means to experience SSA and simultaneously live a covenant life of faith and hope within the bounds the Lord has set. It is a place to learn how others have found strength, resolve, and peace within themselves, their families, and other men who share a common bond in brotherhood.In this sense, Men Finding Peace accepts and adopts the mission of North Star International* to empower individuals and families, addressing sexual orientation or gender identity issues, to genuinely and joyfully live the Gospel of Jesus Christ, and to keep sacred covenants.We recognize that SSA is a complex subject often causing great inner conflict and struggle. We value the power of community as a priority in finding strength and peace, and in building relationships that enrich our personal and spiritual lives. Our group offers a place of service and mentorship where we can all grow together in understanding. Men need other men. They need friendships that lead to true brotherhood in a safe environment. During our meetings, we openly discuss God’s grace and power in our lives without apprehension or apology, and without the intent to change or convert others. Unconditional love and respect for our fellow men are considered sacred, and the opinions and experiences of others present opportunities to learn.For those who have never attended a support group, just walking through the door many require great courage. Each member remembers that first step, but each member also remembers the comfort at the realization that he was not alone and that support and help are available. This is an open group, where any man willing to abide by the participation agreement is invited to attend without fear of being called on or called out. Every participant has the right to remain a silent observer or to share his experiences as impressed. Complete confidentiality is required from all attending and participating in this group. This, along with personal safety, must be respected and upheld by everyone who attends

Name: Pathways Real Life Recovery
Resource Description:
Pathways Real Life Recovery understands the numerous challenges that the LGBTQ+ community go through living in a heteronormative world, and it be even more challenging in the super-conservative state of Utah. Many gay people clash with loved ones due to their identity, and even years later the pain can linger. Sometimes, it’s a close friend or family cutting off all ties, or in other times, it’s bitter words and vitriol spewed in the heat of the moment that can't be forgotten.

Regardless if you seek therapy for issues related to your LGBT status or not, it is imperative you feel supported and able to speak freely in order to benefit from the therapeutic experience. This is especially true for those confronted with the double stigma of mental health issues and LGBT orientation. Pathways is an LGBT counselor in Utah for teens and adults who are seeking professional counseling. We can help you become confident and give you the tools to deal with life’s struggles in a manner that is respectful, affirming, supportive, and non-judgmental.

If you're considering therapy and want to speak with someone who is compassionate, of the specific issues affecting the LGBTQ+ community, contact Pathways for a free assessment. We accept most insurance.

What is LGBTQ+ Counseling?


While an individual’s gender identity or sexual orientation may not be a source of distress, individuals who identify as Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, and Transgender may find the stigma associated with living as a minority to be a source of anxiety and stress. Finding a mental health professional or counselor who is familiar with the challenges that the LGBTQ+ community often face is critical to achieving success in therapy.

Research has shown that LGBTQ+ individuals are at a higher risk of facing problems such as substance abuse disorders, anxiety, and depression due to the stress, bullying, and/or stigmatization from peers, family members, classmates, and even co-workers. LGBTQ+ individuals may also experience issues such as:

- Difficulty understanding gender identity or sexual orientation
- Issues related to LGBTQ+ parents
- Dealing with fear or trauma following hate crimes
- Lack of courage to come out and disclose to family and close friends
- Coping with discrimination and oppression
- Parenting and guiding an LGBTQ+ child
- Risk of suicidal ideation
- Gender transition challenges
- Bullying and victimization at school
- LGBTQ+ Treatment Services

We've anchored our gay-friendly counseling services on inclusivity and bringing change from within. Our treatment services include, but are not limited to:

Group Therapy: Group is a powerful treatment approach. It gives you an opportunity to listen to real life experiences and know that you are not alone. When you listen and interact with people going through the same problems that prompted you to seek therapy, you become more hopeful about achieving full recovery. You will get relevant feedback or honest testimonials that will inspire you to do things differently or nurture a positive perspective on life. In fact, you'll also benefit immensely from the new solutions and ideas you'll learn from these group counseling sessions.

Sexual Assault Therapy: The LGBTQ+ community is at an increased risk of facing sexual assault as they're often marginalized and suffer higher rates of poverty and stigma. Bisexual women and transgender individuals within the LGBTQ+ community are at a higher risk of encountering sexual violence, especially during their childhood. According to a 2015 Transgender survey conducted in the U.S., 47% of transgender individuals have been sexually assaulted in their lifetimes. We help both adolescent survivors and adults overcome these traumatic experiences and move forward with a life full of purpose. 

Couples Counseling: LGBTQ+ individuals experience the same relationship challenges and concerns in life common among all people, such as spending quality time together, the in-laws, money, and are subject to additional daily stressors such as low self-esteem and workplace stress. This can cause massive strain to your relationship, especially if both of you are struggling with these stressors or inner struggles. Our competent team will provide you and your partner with the skills and tools you need to maintain a healthy, loving relationship. This is great for couples who desire privacy and discretion in handling their personal issues.

Addiction Treatment: While addiction is used as a way of coping with everyday stressors among the general population, LGBTQ+ individuals may use it as a mechanism for numbing prejudice, legal obstacles, and discrimination. Our empowerment and solution-based treatment services help our clients learn to love and appreciate themselves and resolve the issues that lead them to want to use in the first place. We provide our clients with the right tools to enable them to value their self-worth and realize that they don't need to use drugs and alcohol in order to cope with their problems.

Family Counseling: Research has proven that LGBTQ+ individuals who receive support and guidance from their family members have significantly better mental health and physical wellbeing. The primary objectives of the family counseling treatment service are to help family members understand that lack of support can be regarded as rejection and can cause serious health problems to their LGBTQ+ loved ones. We help families learn new ways of showing support to their LGBTQ+ family members. The treatment service is not focused on changing deeply-held family beliefs or values. Instead, we help parents, families, and caregivers understand the value of supporting their loved ones, and teach them how to do it.

Trauma Therapy: LGBTQ+ individuals, especially teens who undergo frequent discrimination on a daily basis may end up developing internalized homophobia. This is a dangerous state that can lead to self-hatred and internal shame. Addressing psychological injuries inflicted on lesbians and gays is critical. When an LGBTQ+ child gets insulted for being different, they sustain psychological scars that would last a lifetime if not addressed. Our practitioners will help you or your child recover from such trauma, enabling you to lead a normal life.

Treatment for LGBTQ+ Teens: LGBTQ+ youth are coming out at earlier and earlier ages. Some youth not capable of dealing with the discrimination and bullying faced and may consider suicide as a solution to end their suffering. Our experienced counselors help teens deal with various issues such as family rejection, gender nonconformity, substance abuse, suicide ideation, and violence. We can help teens deal with these issues and help them to love themselves for who they are and give them the skills needed to tackle their difficulties in a productive manner.

Self-Esteem: The LGBTQ+ community faces a special kind of abuse and discrimination. Studies have shown that individuals who are victimized continuously and abused are likely to develop suicidal thoughts. Hence, it is dangerous to nurse unhealthy beliefs about yourself, and you should seek therapy before it becomes dangerous to you and your family. The negative things that naysayers say and do to you are not permanent or impermeable to change. With proper guidance, you can become more positive about life and eventually dissuade the suicidal thoughts.

Name: Peculiar - Allies and Appetizers
Resource Description: Mission Statement: To create safe spaces, filled with great conversation and a new understanding of how to better love and respect our LGBTQ+ family.

Name: Peculiar Journal
Resource Description:
Peculiar is a queer literary journal showcasing prose, poetry, art, and photography. With our roots in the Mormon stronghold of Provo, Utah, peculiar began as a way to recognize the creative talents of the often-overlooked queer community within Utah’s unique culture. As our journal has grown over the past few years—and our staff has begun setting roots nationwide—we’ve decided to broaden the scope of peculiar to include queer voices from anywhere and everywhere. No matter how far you are or how quietly you whisper, know that we hear you.
​
​In our first issue, co-editor-in-chief Aaron Gates wrote the following in his foreword: “To belong, isn't that what we are fighting for, constantly? Every day a wave surges against us, telling us we are too different, telling us we have no place, telling us that something is wrong with us. No one can tell you what you are worth; that is for you to decide.” So we hope you'll decide to be brave. To be strong. To be beautiful.


​This journal celebrates the dazzling diversity of us all. Share your stories with us. Read the stories of others. Take part in something glorious, no matter how peculiar.

Name: Peculiar Stories
Resource Description: Peculiar Stories is an opportunity to share your personal stories and/or insight on your experiences as a member of the LGBTQ+ community. Our community is strengthened as a whole when we share these stories. These stories are intended to bring awareness, change, and ultimately save the lives of our LGBTQ+ youth and community. We are grateful for the courage and the vulnerability shown here as well as the example given. Please honor these stories. They are sacred.

Name: Planned Parenthood Association of Utah
Resource Description: Planned Parenthood Association of Utah shares the vision of an equitable world articulated by the Planned Parenthood Federation of America: where sexual and reproductive rights are basic human rights, where access to health care doesn't depend on who you are and where you live, and where every person has the opportunity to choose their own path to a healthy and meaningful life. Our mission is to empower Utahns of all ages to make informed choices about their sexual health, to ensure access to affordable, quality health care and education, and protect their right to do so.‍

Name: Pre-Teen Support Group
Resource Description: Our Preteen Group is open to all LGBTQ+ and LGBTQ+ affirming youth ages 10-14. We give our preteens a monitored platform to communicate with each other throughout the week and a fixed opportunity to reach out for mutual support from their peers. This allows our preteens to communicate and build a bond with each other, as well as CPC volunteers, for ongoing support and a sense of belonging outside of our Tuesday night group.

Name: Prepare Online Community
Resource Description: This group provides fellowship for LGBTQ people who desire to attend the LDS church and are supportive of everyone whether they're in a same-sex relationship, an opposite-sex relationship, or celibate/abstinent.

Name: Pride of Southern Utah
Resource Description:
Together we can make a change.

Pride of Southern Utah is a grass roots grown non-profit group of who wants to see a change. A change of attitude, acceptance, perspective and love within and surrounding the LGBTQ+ community. Pride of Southern Utah has partnered with A.R.T.S. Inc. as our fiscal partner which gives us non-profit status. Every Dollar, every cent for that matter goes back into the festival and the LGBTQ+ community. While we might be small, we are big in heart, determination and might. Together we can make a change. But we need your help. Whether you are a vendor, volunteer, entertainer or a sponsor we hope that you will join us. Thank you for time and care. 

Who we are: Pride of Southern Utah is a non-profit organization founded on the belief that everyone belongs. Whether you are a member of the LGBTQ+ community or one of our Allies, we want to serve you.   

Philosophy: Build a better, stronger and more cohesive community in Southern Utah. One that feels safe, one that is active and one that offers information and resources.
Address: 307 North Main Street, St. George, UT, 84770

Name: Progressive Paths Therapy
Resource Description:
Welcome to Progressive Paths Therapy! Does it feel like you can’t control your anxiety no matter how hard you try?

Are you feeling hopeless, isolated and not your usual self?

Are you going through a faith crisis, shift, or transition?

Does it feel like your marriage/couple relationship is breaking down?

Are you seeking for a healthier, closer family relationship?

Are you struggling with problematic or out of control sexual behavior?

Have you tried to solve the problems in your life on your own and realized you need help from someone else?

If you answered yes to any of these questions, then you have made the right choice by being here.

And we know this is hard. You've likely been debating seeking help for months, if not years. But we are so glad you found us and have taken the courageous step of being here.

Name: Project Rainbow
Resource Description:
Project Rainbow works to promote LGBTQ+ visibility throughout Utah and foster inclusivity in every corner of the state.

Flag Campaigns

Project Rainbow’s largest fundraiser is our flag campaigns. We stake flags in front of thousands of homes and businesses across Utah each year to celebrate the various pride festivals and events that take place throughout the State. 

Community Fund

The Project Rainbow Community Fund helps finance events or projects that align with our mission to “promote LGBTQ+ visibility throughout Utah.” Individuals, groups, and organizations can apply for grants ranging from $100-$7,000.

Transgender Day of Remembrance

For the week of Transgender Day of Remembrance (November 20) Project Rainbow stakes transgender pride flags along the Wasatch front from Ogden to Provo. Transgender Day of Remembrance (TDOR) is a day to increase visibility for the transgender community and to memorialize the countless transgender individuals who are murdered every year in acts of transphobia. Stand in solidarity with your trans friends, family members, and neighbors by displaying a flag this year for TDOR!

Name: Provo Pride
Resource Description: We are the Provo Pride Council, a non-profit corporation organized to act as a community resource and symbol of hope and pride for residents of Utah County who may identify as gay, lesbian, bisexual, pansexual, transgender, transsexual, queer, questioning, intersex, intergender, asexual, etc. (abbreviated as LGBTQ or LGBT for simplicity).MISSIONOur mission is to support and celebrate the LGBTQ community in Provo and Utah County and foster understanding and ties with the larger community through a Pride Festival and other outreach programs. We affirm the equality, dignity, and right to self-determination of all people.VISIONWe aim to improve our support for the LGBTQ and ally community in Utah County by expanding our outreach programs, holding a Pride Parade in addition to the Festival, building an LGBTQ Center, providing help for the homeless youth population and preventing more homeless youth through education, and developing mutually beneficial ties with sister Pride Festivals and local businesses, non-profit organizations, performers and artists, and the community at large.‍

QUAC is the largest LGBTS sports club in Utah. QUAC offers swimmers and water polo players of all abilities a supportive and safe environment to improve their skills, get some exercise, meet people with similar interests and, if they so choose, the opportunity to compete. Whether you are interested in swimming, multi-sports, or water polo; whether you’re a former competitor or can barely doggy paddle, QUAC has something to offer. Come join us at practice and get involved with one of the biggest and friendliest sports groups in Utah! QUAC is also a Learn to Swim Program in cooperation and with grants from USMS ​Swimming Saves Lives Foundation.
Address: Fairmont Aquatic Center, 1044 East Sugarmont Drive, Salt Lake City, UT 84106

Name: Queer Community Allies
Resource Description:
Local GSA Support
We support GSAs (gay straight alliances/gender sexuality alliances; student-led with a teacher-staff-counselor advisor) in local high schools. Posters, stickers, flags, buttons, masks, wrapped snacks, books, funds for supplies, crafting items, board games, cards, guest visits from affirming adults, contacts from local businesses who can partner for donations… If they don't have the resources for success, we try to help.

Classroom Decor & Educator Supplies
Teachers often ask us for buttons to distribute to faculty-friends and students and for posters, stickers and flags for their classrooms. If you’re a teacher who would like some items, reach out! We’d be happy to gift you some!

Community Events
We love going to Pride, joining other organizations at various city community nights, being involved with other local youth efforts, and hosting events to talk with educators and parents who want to learn more about supporting their queer family members, students, and comunity youth.

Community Swag
We love sharing swag from our neighbor organizations! Thank you Pride Center, HRC Utah, Equality Utah, and Encircle for giving us calendars, chapstick, stickers, pamphlets, flags, glow bracelets, and more to distribute to our teens and at local events. We love seeing rainbow swag around town, from any group!

Name: So You're Mormon and Gay
Resource Description:
Hi, I'm Kelly! I'm 29 years old, born and raised in the San Francisco Bay Area, and currently living and working in Salt Lake City. I am the youngest in a family of five and was spoiled and loved like crazy (the youngest child spot is definitely the best in my opinion). I love being outside, traveling, and all sports, especially basketball (go Warriors!). I played basketball at Lehigh University during my undergrad and then went on to graduate school at BYU. I joined the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in 2010 when I was 19, served a mission in Nagoya, Japan (日本が大好き!), and occassionally attend my ward in Salt Lake. Oh, and yes, I'm gay!


I wanted to create this blog to share my own story and the stories of my LGBTQ Mormon friends. When I started to realize I might be gay (it only took me 23 years to realize my "really close friendships" and "girl crushes" might be something more...), I scoured the internet for everything I could find on the topic of Mormonism and homosexuality; I had no idea what to do! There wasn't much (as helpful as the gospel topics essay is...). I was lucky to meet several other gay, Mormon friends and get the help and support I needed. I realized not everyone is as lucky.


So, I want to share my friends and their stories! I hope this blog will help people see there aren't just two options when it comes to being gay and Mormon: leaving the church or staying single and celibate the rest of your life. There are many more options than that, and I'm excited to share them here with you. This blog will have stories of people fully in the church, fully out of the church, and everywhere in between. Please feel free to reach out if you'd like to have a personal conversation about anything posted here!

Name: Stockton Powers Memorial Scholarship
Resource Description:
GENERAL INFO

The Stockton Powers Memorial Scholarship is available to those who apply for themselves or for those who believe there is someone who is deserving of this scholarship. The scholarship may be applied to tuition cost, book fees, housing, educational tools, and daily expenses. Recipient will receive a certain dollar amount according to needs*. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA

High School Senior to 25 years of age

Furthering your education

Utah applicants only

Maintain a GPA of 2.8 or above 

WHY WE DO ITStockton was born in Salt Lake City, UT on May 5, 1999. He was a long-awaited blessing for our family. Stockton was very adventurous. Whatever he loved, he gave 110%. He loved to swim, play guitar and sing. He was brilliant at these things and truly found his place doing them. When Stockton was 13 years old, he showed our family just how courageous he was when he came out to our family and told us that he was gay. This of course didn't change the way we loved and cared for him, but it did change the way others in our community treated him. Stockton was often more worried about the way others felt than his own feelings, even when he was hurting inside. He was the first to offer a hug to anyone who needed one and was a friend to everyone. He was such an awesome hugger! Although Stockton was deeply loved by his family, he didn't feel that in other places and communities. On June 27, 2016 we lost Stockton to suicide. We will never be the same. Our hearts are in pieces. There needs to be a change, not only for our Stockton, but for all the other children who feel they don't have a place because they are seen as different. Our goal is to raise awareness around suicide, not only in the LGBT community, but for everyone affected by this ever-increasing tragedy.

Name: Utah Coalition Against Sexual Assault - LGBTQ Coordinating Counsel
Resource Description:
Our Statewide LGBTQ Coordinating Council Advisory Council (Council) is a permanent advisory council located within the Utah Coalition Against Sexual Assault (UCASA). It was established by a vote of the Board of Directors in 2017 to ensure that LGBTQ survivors and victims of sexual violence are represented in victim services organizations, institutions, and partnerships that serve sexual violence survivors statewide. This includes but is not limited to:

Ensuring adequate representation of LGBTQ survivors in all Sexual Assault Response Teams (SARTs) statewide.

Ensuring that LGBTQ-affirming training is provided statewide to sexual violence programs, law enforcement, and any other institution that interacts with sexual violence survivors.

Ensuring that print, online, and others forms of information are available online to improve services for LGBTQ survivors of sexual violence.

Producing LGBTQ-affirming materials for distribution statewide with a focus on rural, underserved, and culturally-specific programs and communities.

Assist organizations serving LGBTQ survivors to understand the unique cultural, historical, and institutional barriers faced by LGBTQ survivors in accessing services.

As the Council expands we expect that members of the Council and the community will identify additional goals and objectives that cannot currently be anticipated by our organization. 
The Council addresses many important issues of interest to LGBTQ people and our allies. The Council utilizes the existing infrastructure of UCASA to define issues of concern to the LGBTQ community and find innovative ways of utilizing UCASA’s resources to help address these issues. Council members meet monthly and provide quarterly status updates to the Board of Directors. 

We recognize that sexual orientation and gender identity are integral aspects of our lives and communities. The Council works to ensure that our policies, communications, and actions reflect this fact. We further recognize that the LGBTQ is not a monolithic, homogenous community and that our work must reflect the incredible vibrancy, uniqueness, and strength of the LGBTQ community.

Members are encouraged to act as a conduit for the broader LGBTQ community and to help ensure that UCASA is meeting the needs of all of our LGBTQ constituents. Throughout their time on the Council, members may serve on subcommittees and are encouraged the embrace their role representing the organization. The Council reports to the Board of Directors and will regular progress reports as well as give recommendations for improvements to UCASA’s programming and goals.

Name: Utah Fertility Clinic
Resource Description:
LGBTQ Family Building

Everyone’s journey to parenthood is unique, and we strive to make this experience as seamless and comfortable as possible.  Whether you need donor sperm, donor eggs, or a gestational carrier (surrogate), our reproductive specialists and staff will help you to navigate the process to best fit your needs.  LGBTQ family building may involve intrauterine inseminations or In Vitro Fertilization, and we welcome the opportunity to help all couples or individuals conceive.

Fertility Treatment for Lesbian Couples


Treatment for lesbian couples is typically intrauterine inseminations (IUI) or In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) using donor sperm.  A consultation with one of our physicians and review of both partners’ medical history can help determine the most optimal treatment options. Questions to consider are whose eggs will be used and who will carry the baby.

Treatment for Gay Couples


Treatment for gay couples involves In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) and third-party reproduction, which entails egg donation and gestational surrogacy.  Beginning with a fertility consultation, your physician will guide you into the initial necessary steps. A semen analysis and required FDA testing is completed on one or both partners whose sperm will be utilized. Egg donors can be known (family members or friends) or can be chosen through our anonymous egg donor database.  Utah Fertility Center has an online database with a substantial number of egg donors.  We also work with many gestational carrier agencies and are happy to work with independent matches as well. Your attentive third party coordinator will work closely with you and your physician as they walk you through every step of your journey.

To learn more about our LGBTQ family building in St. George, Pleasant Grove, Salt Lake, Ogden, and Park City we encourage you to contact us today.

Name: WSU Matthew Shepherd Scholarship
Resource Description:
The purpose of this endowed scholarship is to support students at Weber State University who identify as a sexual or gender minority as well as their allies. It is a goal of this scholarship to educate individuals about issues concerning sexual and gender minorities and to create an atmosphere of support and nurturing for all students at Weber State University. 

Scholarship applications are taken during Spring Semester and scholarships are awarded for the academic year starting in Fall Semester. Scholarship Awards can cover resident tuition, books, fees and other educational expenses. 

The Weber State University Matthew Shepard Scholarship strives to: 

Build awareness of the academic achievements and community service of sexual and gender minority students at Weber State University. 

 Encourage recipients to complete their studies and become an engaged, supportive community leader.

Raise the hopes and aspirations of sexual and gender minority students, many of whom strive against great obstacles. 

Build a healthier and more positive understanding of sexual and gender minorities both among themselves and in the public mind.

Resource Description:
#### Mental health therapy specializing in queerness, sex therapy, and Mormon faith transitions.

Queerness, faith transitions, religious trauma, and sex. I can (and do) talk about these topics all day. Any one of these issues can seem overwhelming and impossible to deal with. As a therapist who has dealt with these issues myself, I bring both professional and personal experience to help you move forward. I know every person's story and life is unique and I won't project my experiences on you. However, you won't have to explain the "Mormon lingo" or worry that I won't understand the unique issues queer individuals face in a heteronormative and cisgender world.

When we meet, I want to make sure I understand you holistically and that you feel heard. I then work collaboratively with you to create a personalized plan moving forward. I can draw from a wide variety of modalities and techniques to find what suits you best and will hold a safe space for you as you explore, grow, and heal.

I look forward to working with you as you navigate the challenges that life brings. I provide a therapeutic environment that is nurturing, safe, and free from judgment, and bring skills and experience to make it all feel just a little bit easier. Contact me today to get on my schedule.
